about: One entry per Device Hub Pro Controls row (ControlsRow in Sources/DeviceHubProApp/DeviceSettingsPanelModel.swift), in its order: a row of the Android Controls panel, of a simulator's Device Hub cards or of a physical iPhone's panel. label is the row's title in the Controls inspector (null for untitled value/button rows). A platform key (android, ios) means the row is offered there; a row without it is not. Per platform: verifier lists the rows of that platform's verifier app (android/verifier, ios/verifier) that observe it; sameTitle means that verifier row's title is the label verbatim; label overrides the shared label on that platform; why says why an empty verifier list is empty. ios also says which targets the row acts on (simulator; device: a physical iPhone that lists the row's CoreDevice feature; ApplePhysicalControlsLiveTests round-trips each such row on the test iPhone), what the verifier observes (effect: what apps see; key: the written value; note: nothing an app can read, the row says so) and privateApi when the write relies on undocumented behaviour. A row's surface (optional) says where else it is reachable: since 2026-10-06 every settings row of the Controls panels is also a Device menu item (Android too), and the fingerprint touch, the simulator's memory warning and Android's low memory are a panel row and a menu item each. menuRows lists what only a menu, the stage or a toolbar button carries (Sensors, Simulate, Orientation, Clipboard, the fold strip, Resize, Add Sample Data, Slow Animations): no ControlsRow, but the same platform keys, so the verifier rows that observe them stay mapped; surface says where each one is. Whether a device family (Wear OS, TV, Apple TV ...) can work a row is a refinement of these platform keys and lives in ControlsRow.availability(on:) (Sources/DeviceHubProApp/ControlsRowAvailability.swift, tested by ControlsRowAvailabilityTests). Checked by ControlsRowManifestTests (Swift), ControlsRowsManifestTest (JUnit) and IOSVerifierRegistryTests (Swift).

android.why: Throughput needs a timed transfer against a server the verifier does not have (the opt-in live test ShapingLiveTests measures it from the host); the caption under Speed names the data path, which the verifier reads. The row shows only on debuggable (tc-capable) emulator builds.

ios.why: Routes the simulator's sound to a Mac audio device (devicectl device settings audio --output-device); the verifier has no audio-route row: an app reads the simulated speaker whichever Mac device plays it.

Routes the simulator's microphone to a Mac audio device (devicectl device settings audio --input-device); the verifier has no audio-route row: an app reads the simulated microphone whichever Mac device records it.

ios.why: Starts the target app (simctl launch, devicectl device process launch); the verifier has no row for being launched: it only shows what the system tells a running app.
Ends the target app (simctl terminate, devicectl device process terminate); the verifier cannot report its own end.

rows.label: Memory warning
rows.surface: Controls ▸ App conditions ▸ Memory warning and Device ▸ Simulate Memory Warning (⇧⌘M)

ios.why: Trusts a root certificate in the simulator's keychain (simctl keychain add-root-cert); the verifier reads no trust store.
Removes the simulator's keychain items (simctl keychain reset); the verifier keeps no keychain item to watch.
Puts back the settings other rows change (appearance, text size, the accessibility switches, Liquid Glass, the status bar override, the location); those rows' verifier rows show each result.
